definitions.text: any natural or legal person, public authority, public corporation, non-governmental organization, agency or any other body or entity which alone or jointly with others determines the purposes and means of the processing of personal data

a natural or legal person, public authority or other entity established by or under any written law, which processes personal data on behalf of the controller; a separate entity or person from the controller and not under the hierarchical control of the controller, and excludes internal processing such as one department processing for another or an employee processing on behalf of their employer

any operation performed on personal data including but not limited to collection, storage, preservation, alteration, retrieval, disclosure, transmission, making available, erasure, destruction of, consultation, alignment, combination, or the carrying out of logical or arithmetical operations on personal data

personal data revealing racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious or philosophical beliefs; genetic data; biometric data for the purpose of uniquely identifying a natural person; data concerning health; data concerning a natural person's sex life or sexual orientation; personal data relating to offences, criminal proceedings and convictions; or personal data relating to a child
any freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous indication by way of a written declaration or an affirmative action signifying a data subject's agreement to the processing of his personal data
a natural person who is below the age of sixteen years
any act or omission that results in accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorized disclosure of, or access to, personal data transmitted, stored or otherwise processed
the person designated or appointed under section 20 of this Act

a Ministry, any Department or Provincial Council, local authority, statutory body or any institution established by any written law, or a Ministry, Department or other authority or institution established or created by a Provincial Council
a country prescribed under section 26 for the purpose of cross-border data flow
the movement of personal data out of the territory of Sri Lanka for the purpose of processing personal data in a third country
any employee, consultant, agent, affiliate or any person who is contracted by the processor to process personal data

clauses.title: Obligation to process personal data in a lawful manner
clauses.verbatim_text: The processing of personal data shall be lawful if a controller is in compliance with - (a) any condition specified in Schedule I hereto; (b) any condition specified in Schedule II hereto in the case of processing special categories of personal data; (c) all the conditions specified in Schedule III hereto in the case of processing personal data based on the consent of the data subject under item (a) of Schedule I or under item (a) of Schedule II hereto; or (d) all the conditions specified in Schedule IV hereto in the case of processing personal data in respect of criminal investigations.
clauses.simplified_text: Processing is lawful only if it satisfies a lawful basis: any Schedule I condition; additionally a Schedule II condition where special-category data is processed; all Schedule III conditions where the chosen basis is consent; or all Schedule IV conditions for criminal-investigation processing. A gateway clause routing to different Schedules by data type and chosen basis.

clauses.title: Obligation to define a purpose for personal data processing
clauses.verbatim_text: (1) Every controller shall, ensure that personal data is processed for a - (a) specified; (b) explicit; and (c) legitimate, purposes and such personal data shall not be further processed in a manner which is incompatible with such purposes. (2) Subject to the provisions of section 10 of this Act, further processing of such personal data by a controller for archiving purposes in the public interest, scientific research, historical research or statistical purposes shall not be considered to be incompatible with the initial purposes referred to in paragraphs (a), (b) and (c) of subsection (1).
clauses.simplified_text: The processing purpose must be specified, explicit, and legitimate, and data must not later be reused incompatibly with that purpose. Reuse for public-interest archiving, scientific/historical research, or statistics is deemed compatible - but only if s.10's safeguards are also met.

clauses.title: Obligation to confine personal data processing to the defined purpose
clauses.verbatim_text: Every controller shall ensure that personal data that is processed shall be - (a) adequate; (b) relevant; and (c) proportionate, to the extent as is necessary in relation to the purpose for which such data shall be collected or processed.
clauses.simplified_text: Data minimisation: the personal data collected or processed must be adequate, relevant, and proportionate relative to the s.6 purpose. No independent meaning without a defined purpose to judge against.

clauses.title: Obligation to ensure accuracy
clauses.verbatim_text: Every controller shall ensure that personal data that is processed shall be - (a) accurate; and (b) kept up to date, with every reasonable step being taken to erase or rectify any inaccurate or outdated personal data, without undue delay.
clauses.simplified_text: Data must be accurate and current, and the controller has a standing, proactive duty to erase or rectify inaccurate/outdated data without undue delay - independent of any data subject request.

clauses.title: Obligation to limit the period of retention
clauses.verbatim_text: Every controller shall ensure that personal data that is being processed shall be kept in a form which permits identification of data subjects only for such period as may be necessary or required for the purposes for which such personal data is processed: Provided however, subject to the provisions of section 10 of this Act, a controller may store personal data for longer periods in so far as the personal data shall be processed further for archiving purposes in the public interest, scientific research, historical research or statistical purposes.
clauses.simplified_text: Identifiable personal data may be kept only as long as necessary for its purpose; once no longer needed in identifiable form it should be deleted or de-identified. Longer retention is permitted for archiving/research/statistical purposes, but only subject to s.10.

clauses.title: Obligation to maintain integrity and confidentiality
clauses.verbatim_text: Every controller shall ensure integrity and confidentiality of personal data that is being processed, by using appropriate technical and organizational measures including encryption, pseudonymisation, anonymisation or access controls or such other measures as may be prescribed so as to prevent the - (a) unauthorized or unlawful processing of personal data; or (b) loss, destruction or damage of personal data.
clauses.simplified_text: The controller must protect data with appropriate technical and organizational measures (encryption, pseudonymisation, anonymisation, access controls named as examples, not a closed list) to prevent both unauthorized/unlawful processing and loss/destruction/damage. Spans two CIA-triad properties; depended upon by s.6(2) and s.9's exemptions.

clauses.annotation_notes: CACR DECISION: the four named techniques are keywords, NOT attributes, because the Act says 'including' - illustrative, not each mandatory. Counting them as required would make CACR over-demand. Attributes are the two prevention outcomes plus technical/organizational measures existing. Inbound edges from s.6-u2 and s.9-u2 derived at load time; s.10 is the 'depended-upon' node in the three-way cluster.

clauses.title: Accountability in the processing of personal data (Data Protection Management Programme)
clauses.verbatim_text: (1) It shall be the duty of every controller to implement internal controls and procedures (the 'Data Protection Management Programme') that - (a) establishes and maintains duly catalogued records to demonstrate the manner in which the implementation of the data protection obligations referred to in sections 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11 are carried out; (b) is designed on the basis of structure, scale, volume and sensitivity of processing activities; (c) provides for appropriate safeguards based on data protection impact assessments specified in section 24; (d) is integrated into the governance structure of the controller; (e) establishes internal oversight mechanisms; (f) has a mechanism to receive complaints, conduct inquiries and identify personal data breaches; (g) is updated based on periodic monitoring and assessments; and (h) facilitates the exercise of rights of data subjects under sections 13, 14, 15, 16 and 18, for the purpose of complying with the obligations referred to in sections 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11. (2) The Authority shall from time to time issue guidelines in respect of the Data Protection Management Programme.
clauses.simplified_text: The meta-obligation of Part I: the controller must build and maintain an internal governance system (the DPMP) that documents, oversees, and continuously updates how it complies with all the other Part I obligations (ss.5-11). Accountability infrastructure - record-keeping, governance integration, complaint/breach detection, periodic review - rather than a data-handling rule itself.

clauses.title: Additional obligations of the processors
clauses.verbatim_text: (1) Where a processor is engaged in processing activities on behalf of the controller, the processor shall - (a) ensure that processing activities are carried out only on the written instructions of the controller; (b) ensure that its personnel are bound by contractual obligations on confidentiality and secrecy by the implementation of appropriate technical and organizational measures; (c) facilitate the controller to carry out compliance audits, including inspections upon the written request of the controller; and (d) upon the written instructions of the controller, erase existing copies of personal data or return all personal data to the controller after the completion of the provision of services. (2) Where a processor fails to comply with paragraph (a) or determines the purposes and means of processing by itself, such processor shall be deemed to be a controller in respect of such processing. (3) Where a processor engages a sub processor, the provisions of this section shall apply to such sub processor. (4) Where a sub processor fails to fulfil its obligations, the processor shall be liable to the controller. (5) 'personnel' means any employee, consultant, agent, affiliate or any person contracted by the processor to process personal data.
clauses.simplified_text: Four processor duties: act only on written instructions; bind personnel to confidentiality; support compliance audits; delete/return data on instruction at end of service. Subsection (2) reclassifies a processor as a controller if it exceeds instructions or independently sets purposes. Subsections (3)-(4) extend obligations down a sub-processing chain with the processor liable for sub-processor failures.

clauses.title: Personal data breach notifications
clauses.verbatim_text: (1) In the event of a personal data breach, a controller shall notify the Authority, regarding such personal data breach in such form, manner and within such period of time as may be determined by rules made under this Act. (2) The Authority shall provide for - (a) the circumstances where the Authority shall be notified of such data breach; (b) the circumstances where the affected data subject shall be notified; and (c) the form, and manner of making such notification, and information which shall be provided in such notification relating to the data breach, by way of rules made under this Act.
clauses.simplified_text: On a personal data breach, the controller must notify the Authority - but the Act itself does not specify timeline, form, or trigger conditions. Those are deferred to Authority rules under subsection (2). Unlike GDPR Art. 33's explicit 72-hour window, s.23 sets no concrete number in the primary legislation; the operative detail lives in rules that currently exist only in draft.

clauses.title: Personal data protection impact assessments
clauses.verbatim_text: (1) Where a Controller intends to carry out any processing which involves - (a) a systematic and extensive evaluation of personal data or special categories of personal data including profiling; (b) a systematic monitoring of publicly accessible areas or telecommunication networks; or (c) a processing activity as may be determined by way of rules taking into consideration the scope and associated risks, such controller shall, prior to such processing, carry out a personal data protection impact assessment to ascertain the impact of the intended processing on the obligations under Part I and the rights of data subjects under Part II. (2) The assessment shall contain measures and safeguards to mitigate any risk of harm. (3) The controller shall seek the assistance of the Data Protection Officer, where designated. (4) The controller shall conduct a fresh assessment whenever there is any change in methodology, technology or process. (5) The controller shall submit the assessment to the Authority and provide any other information on request.
clauses.simplified_text: Before certain higher-risk processing, the controller must conduct a formal DPIA. Three triggers: (a) systematic extensive evaluation/profiling; (b) systematic monitoring of publicly accessible areas or telecom networks; (c) a rule-designated high-risk activity. The DPIA must document mitigations, involve the DPO if designated, be redone on material change, and be submitted to the Authority. Trigger (b) is the most literal fit for the FleetTrack location-tracking scenario.

clauses.title: Cross-border data flow
clauses.verbatim_text: (1) Where a public authority processes personal data as controller or processor, such personal data shall be processed only in Sri Lanka and shall not be processed in a third country, unless the Authority classifies categories permitted in a third country pursuant to an adequacy decision. (2) [Minister's adequacy-decision process, reviewed at least every two years.] (3) A controller or processor other than a public authority may process personal data - (a) in a third country prescribed pursuant to an adequacy decision; or (b) in a country not so prescribed, only where it ensures compliance with the obligations under Part I, Part II and ss.20-25 of Part III. (4) [Instruments the Authority may specify for binding safeguards.] (5) In the absence of an adequacy decision or appropriate safeguards, a controller or processor other than a public authority may process personal data outside Sri Lanka if - (a) explicit informed consent; (b) contract necessity; (c) legal claims; (d) public interest as defined in Schedule I item (g); (e) vital-interest emergency; or (f) other prescribed conditions.
clauses.simplified_text: A tiered system differing by actor. Public authorities: data stays in Sri Lanka unless the Authority classifies categories as permitted abroad under an adequacy decision. Private controllers/processors: adequacy-decision countries are fine; non-adequacy countries only if the full Part I/II/20-25 obligation set is independently satisfied; failing both, a narrow list of derogations applies. Cross-border transfer is default-prohibited; permission is the exception that must be affirmatively established.
